A 80-year-old male arrives at the emergency department with a one-hour history of swelling in his lips
and hands. He reports that the swelling began shortly after taking his morning medications, which were
recently adjusted during a primary care visit. His medical history includes diabetes, hypertension, and
hyperlipidemia. He has no known drug allergies and does not use any supplements. On examination,
he exhibits continued facial and lip swelling, causing breathing difficulties. He is subsequently intubated
and administered epinephrine. Which of the following laboratory findings is most likely in this patient?
Answer Choices: (A) Decreased C2 and decreased C4 (B) Decreased C1 inhibitor and normal C4 (C)
Increased C3 and decreased C4 (D) Normal C2 and increased C4 (E) Decreased C1q and normal C4
(F) Increased C2 and increased C4 (G) Increased C1 inhibitor and decreased C4 (H) Normal C1
inhibitor and decreased C3 (I) Normal C2 and decreased C4 (J) Normal C2 and normal C4
 A. Normal C2 and increased C4
B. Decreased C2 and decreased C4
C. Decreased C1q and normal C4
D. Normal C2 and normal C4
E. Increased C3 and decreased C4
F. Decreased C1 inhibitor and normal C4
G. Normal C2 and decreased C4
H. Increased C2 and increased C4
I. Normal C1 inhibitor and decreased C3

J. Increased C1 inhibitor and decreased C4
